title: Unify form primitives: tokens, focus states, and validation microcopy
creator: Sophie Ramirez
description:
Background:
We have multiple ad-hoc implementations of text fields, selects, and toggles across the product. Token usage is inconsistent (multiple gray/neutral tokens used for borders, focus rings vary, validation colors overlap with accent palettes). This causes visual regressions, accessibility drift, and extra implementation work for engineers.

Goal:
Unify the visual and interaction patterns for form primitives (text input, textarea, single-select, multi-select, toggle/switch, checkbox) by defining:
- canonical tokens for border, background, focus ring, placeholder, helper and error states
- clear interaction states (hover, focus, disabled, read-only, invalid, success) with detailed motion/transition guidance
- validation microcopy guidelines and examples for inline vs. summary errors
- accessibility requirements (contrast ratios, focus target size, screen-reader labels and live region behavior)

Scope:
In scope: text fields (single-line + multiline), selects (native-like and custom menu), toggles (switches + checkboxes), validation/error states, helper text behavior, tokens mapping and Figma components.
Out of scope: full overhaul of form layout/grid, date/time pickers, file upload components (these will be follow-ups).

Success metrics:
- All core product screens use the unified tokens and components within 3 sprints after rollout.
- Reduction in design/implementation follow-up tickets for input states by 60% in Q2.
- No regressions in accessibility scan for contrast/focus on sampled pages.

Deliverables:
- Figma component set with updated tokens and interactive prototypes (desktop + mobile).
- Annotated token mapping doc (token name -> hex / token rationale).
- Validation microcopy guide and examples (short, actionable messages; length guidelines).
- Engineering spec with CSS variables, transition timings, and aria guidance.
- Migration checklist and quick fix snippets for legacy components.

Constraints / Trade-offs:
- We want a single neutral border token, but tighter contrast requirements for focus rings force using a more prominent token on low-contrast backgrounds. We'll provide token variants (neutral-1, neutral-1-contrast) and a migration table for contexts.
- Animated focus rings increase perceived latency on low-end devices; motion will be subtle and optional (reduced-motion prefers respected).

Acceptance criteria:
- Figma components exported with tokens and layer naming conventions match tokens doc.
- Engineering implements CSS variables and a small demo page showing each state; automated visual snapshots pass.
- Accessibility audit (a11y checklist) passes for color contrast, keyboard focus order, and SR announcements for validation errors.

Stakeholders:
- Product: Maya Chen (PM), Ravi Patel (PM)
- Engineering: Sarah Lee (Frontend), Omar Haddad (Runtime)
- Design: Sophie Ramirez (owner), Liam O'Connor (assignee)
- QA: Priya Menon

Migration plan (high level):
1) Introduce tokens and new components behind a feature flag.
2) Convert low-risk pages (billing, account settings) to new components first.
3) Run visual diff and a11y checks; iterate on token contrast in place.
4) Remove old tokens/components and update docs.

Artifacts and links:
- Figma: https://figma.com/redwood/design-systems/forms/primitives (working file)
- Token doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DS/Tokens+for+Forms
- Engineering spec (Drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/design/form-primitives-spec.md
- PR template for implementation: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ui-components/pulls
comments: 2026-01-12 — Kickoff: Reviewed inconsistent borders and focus rings across Console routes. Agreed to unify around single neutral token with contrast variant. Maya to confirm product prioritization.

2026-01-15 — Design exploration: Shared three visual directions (soft rounded, crisp square, elevated ring). Team favored soft rounded with a subtle outer focus ring to preserve clarity at small sizes.

2026-01-18 — Accessibility sync: Sarah and Priya raised concerns about placeholder contrast and small target sizes; updated target min height to 40px touch target. Added explicit guidance for reduced-motion media query.

2026-01-22 — Engineering feasibility: Omar flagged that legacy select implementation relies on a third-party library; recommended a compatibility wrapper for transition period. ENG-2041 created for wrapper work.

2026-01-28 — Microcopy workshop: Consolidated validation categories (required, format, server). Drafted guidelines: prefer short imperative phrasing, avoid technical jargon, provide remediation steps when possible.
2026-01-30 — Figma: Uploaded interactive variants and prototype states. Started token rename from neutral-300 -> token.input-border to be more explicit. Link: figma file (above).
2026-02-02 — Design review: PMs approved tokens and microcopy. Action: produce engineering spec and small demo page. Liam to assign follow-up tasks for component props and aria attributes.
2026-02-05 — Blockers: None currently. Next steps: finalize spec, pair with Sarah on CSS variable mapping and identify initial pages for migration.

Implementation notes for engineers: Use CSS variables: --rwd-input-bg, --rwd-input-border, --rwd-input-focus, --rwd-input-placeholder, --rwd-input-helper. Respect prefers-reduced-motion. For selects, provide two modes: native and custom; custom must expose aria-activedescendant and keyboard nav.
qa_checklist: Keyboard access: tab + shift-tab cycles through inputs in visual order
Focus outlines present and meet contrast on all backgrounds
Error messages announced by SR on submit and when input loses focus on invalid
Visual snapshot: no unexpected diffs for migrated pages
Touch target >= 40px on mobile for toggles and inputs
implementation_notes: Provide a feature flag 'forms-unified-primitives' for staged rollout
Include migration snippets in PR description referencing token mapping table
Add unit tests for helper/error text rendering and aria-live region behavior
